faq.q: What happens to blood in the lungs?
faq.a: In the lungs, blood picks up oxygen from the air sacs and gives up carbon dioxide, by diffusion. It goes in dark red and low in oxygen and comes out bright red and full of oxygen.

faq.q: What does the right side of the heart do?
faq.a: The right side receives blood low in oxygen from the body and pumps it to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
asks: Tell me about the right side of the heart

faq.q: Why is the left side of the heart thicker?
faq.a: The left ventricle pumps blood all around the body, which needs much higher pressure than the short trip to the lungs, so its muscle wall is much thicker.
asks: Tell me about the left side of the heart

faq.q: What do body cells take from the blood?
faq.a: Body cells take oxygen and glucose for respiration and give back carbon dioxide and other waste, through the thin walls of capillaries.
asks: Tell me about the body cells

faq.q: Why have two loops instead of one?
faq.a: After the lungs, blood pressure is low. Sending it back to the heart for a second pump means it reaches the body fast and at high pressure. Fish have a single loop; mammals and birds have two.

facts: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice for each complete circuit of the body.
Fish have a single circulation; mammals and birds have a double circulation.
